texts.facts: 3) By way of present application, the applicants have prayed for quashing and setting aside the proceedings of complaint being Criminal Case No.449/2006 filed under the provisions of Sections 7 and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, pending in the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Rajkot. 4) At the instance of respondent No.2, complaint came to be filed alleging that, applicant No.1 was Managing Director and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5437/2021 ORDER DATED: 06/09/2024 Devang Sanatkumar Desai (Managing ... vs State Of Gujarat on 6 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64856513/ 1 undefined applicant No.2 was Director of M/s. Adani Retail Ltd. It is further alleged that, upon analysis of samples taken from Shri Pareshbhai Amrutlal Joshi (accused No.1) by the Food Inspector, Rajkot Mahanagar Palika, it is found that there was misbranded as well as product was adulterated and therefore, it is in clear violation of Rule 32(C) of the PFA Rules. Thereby, the applicants accused have committed an offence under Sections 7 and 16 of the Act.
texts.arguments: 5) Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that, the applicants are Managing Director and Director respectively of M/s. Adani Retail ltd., but they are not connected in any manner with the alleged offence. As per the provisions of Section 17 of the Act, legislature has made the provisions to the effect that, any offence committed under the PFA Act, then the company and its nominated persons shall be liable to prosecute and punish. As per the mandatory provisions of Section 17 and Rule 12(b), the company has already submitted nomination form on 15.02.2005 and one Mr.Parag S. Padrakar is duly nominated as officer on behalf of the company in State of Gujarat for its activities within the purview of the Act. The said communication is produced at Annexure-B and accepted by the authority. He further submitted that, though without making any violation, the applicants have falsely implicated in the offence and proceedings being initiated. Hence, to continue such proceedings against the applicants are nothing, but an abuse of process of law. 5.1) Learned Senior Counsel for the applicants relying on the decision of this Court rendered in case of Pranav V. Adani NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5437/2021 ORDER DATED: 06/09/2024 undefined (Director) & Ors. Vs. State of Gujarat & Anr. [CRMA/3354/2008], submitted that, the same issue has been decided by a coordinate Bench of this Court and therefore, present dispute is squarely covered. Hence, he requested to allow present application. 6) Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has opposed the present application and submitted that, the sample taken for analysis was found misbranded and adulterated and therefore, in violation of Food Adulteration Act, complaint came to be filed against the accused. He has further submitted that, whatever the defense put forward by the applicants, let trial Court be ordered to be decided in accordance with law. In view of the same, present application does not deserve any consideration. 7) Learned APP for the State has also opposed the present application and stated that, in the present case, complaint is filed and trial is going on and hence, this is not a case to quash the proceedings and exercise jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. Therefore, present application may not be entertained. 8) Having heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perusing the record, it appears that, complaint is filed in the court of learned JMFC, Rajkot, wherein no any averment is made qua the applicants that they are directly involved in the day to day activities of the retail outlets and they were involved in manufacturing, purchase and sale. Offences by companies:- .-(1) Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company-(a)(i)the person, if any, who has been nominated under sub-section (2) to be in charge of, and responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company (hereafter in this section referred to as the person responsible), or( ii)where no person has been so nominated, every person who at the time the offence was committed was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company; and(b)the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly:Provided that nothing contained in this sub- section shall render any such person liable to any punishment provided in this Act if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge and that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence. (2)Any company may, by order in writing, authorise any of its directors or managers (such manager being employed mainly in a managerial or supervisory capacity) to exercise all such powers and take all such steps as may be necessary or expedient to prevent the commission by the company of any offence under this Act and may give notice to the Local (Health) Authority, in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed, that it has nominated such director or manager as the person responsible, alongwith the written consent of such director or manager for being so nominated. Explanation .-Where a company has different establishments or branches or different units in any establishment or branch, different persons may be nominated under this sub-section in relation to different establishments or branches or units and the person nominated in relation to any establishment, branch or unit shall be deemed to be the person responsible in respect of such establishment, branch or unit. NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/5437/2021 ORDER DATED: 06/09/2024 undefined (3)The person nominated under sub-section (2) shall, until- (i)further notice cancelling such nomination is received from the company by the Local (Health) Authority; or (ii)he ceases to be a director or, as the case may be, manager of the company; or (iii)he makes a request in writing to the Local (Health) Authority, under intimation to the company, to cancel the nomination [which request shall be complied with by the Local (Health) Authority], whichever is the earliest, continue to be the person responsible :Provided that where such person ceases to be a director or, as the case may be, manager of the company, he shall intimate the fact of such cesser to the Local (Health) Authority:Provided further that where such person makes a Devang Sanatkumar Desai (Managing ... vs State Of Gujarat on 6 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64856513/ 3 request under clause (iii), the Local (Health) Authority shall not cancel such nomination with effect from a date earlier than the date on which the request is made. (4)Notwithstanding anything contained in the foregoing sub- sections, where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company and it is proved that the offence has been committed with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to, any neglect on the part of, any director, manager, secretary or other officer of the company [not being a person nominated under sub- section (2) such director, manager, secretary or other officer shall also be deemed to be guilty of that offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. Explanation .-For the purposes of this section- (a)"company", means any body corporate and includes a firm or other association of individuals; (b)"director", in relation to a firm, means a partner in the firm; and (c)"manager", in relation to a company engaged in hotel industry, includes the person in charge of the catering department of any hotel managed or run by it." 10) In light of the above, nomination under Section 17 of the Act and Rule 12(b) is furnished to Local Health Authority, Ahmedabad, which was accepted by the said authority and one Mr. Parag S. Padrakar is nominated by the company. 12) Considering the judgment of coordinate Bench of this Court rendered in Criminal Misc. Application No.3354/2008 , wherein, the coordinate Bench has been pleased to quash the proceedings on the same set of facts as well as the principle laid down in the case of State of Haryana & Ors. Vs. Bhajanlal & Ors., [1992 Suppl. 1 SCC 2020], this is a fit case to exercise inherent power under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C for quashing of criminal proceedings.
